answer: A scarce-seat auction raises Sybil costs. The protocol keeps a finite grid of identity plots; each new agent must win one unused plot and lock a pearl deposit against it for many epochs. As occupancy grows, a price crystal forms, so the marginal plot costs far more than the first. An attacker who wants a thousand votes must buy a thousand distinct plots on that mesa of limited surface, posting a deposit on each and paying the inflated clearing price. Fresh keypairs do not create extra plots, so influence is bounded by capital and scarcity, not by wallet generation speed.
